i-91/vt.endpoints: Massachusetts state line at Guilford near Brattleboro north to the Canadian border at Derby Line
i-91/vt.description: I-91 runs the full length of eastern Vermont along the Connecticut River, from Brattleboro through White River Junction and St. Johnsbury to the Canadian border at Derby Line. It is a rural corridor with long gaps between services, sustained grades in the Northeast Kingdom, and serious winter weather; White River Junction is the key junction with I-89 for Burlington and Montreal traffic.

i-93/ma.endpoints: I-95 at Canton north through Boston to the New Hampshire state line at Methuen
i-93/ma.description: I-93 is metro Boston's north-south spine, running from I-95 at Canton up the Southeast Expressway through Quincy and downtown Boston, including the O'Neill Tunnel, then north past Woburn to the New Hampshire line. Congestion is heavy for nearly the entire run and the downtown tunnel restricts hazmat loads, so through trucks often route around on I-95 or I-495.

i-93/nh.endpoints: Massachusetts state line at Salem north through Franconia Notch to the Vermont state line near Littleton
i-93/nh.description: I-93 runs the length of New Hampshire from the busy Salem-Manchester-Concord corridor into the White Mountains, where it narrows to a single lane each way as a parkway through Franconia Notch. North of Concord traffic drops off sharply and mountain grades and winter conditions become the main concern; the state's freight activity concentrates around Manchester.

i-93/vt.endpoints: New Hampshire state line near Waterford to its northern terminus at I-91 in St. Johnsbury
i-93/vt.description: Vermont's I-93 is a short rural connector of about 11 miles that climbs from the Connecticut River valley to end at I-91 in St. Johnsbury. It links Boston-bound I-93 traffic with I-91 toward Canada and is a quiet, scenic stretch with no services on the highway itself.

i-95/ct.endpoints: New York state line at Greenwich to the Rhode Island state line at Pawcatuck
i-95/ct.description: I-95 hugs the Connecticut shoreline from Greenwich through Stamford, Bridgeport, and New Haven before the traffic thins east of the Connecticut River toward New London and the Rhode Island line. The southwestern half is one of the most congested truck corridors in the country, with tight urban interchanges and frequent delays between Greenwich and New Haven.

i-95/dc.endpoints: Crosses the southern tip of the District on the Woodrow Wilson Bridge between Virginia and Maryland
i-95/dc.description: I-95 touches the District of Columbia for only about a tenth of a mile, where the Woodrow Wilson Bridge clips the city's southern tip over the Potomac River. Through freight follows I-95 around Washington on the Capital Beltway; no I-95 mainline runs through the city itself.

i-95/de.endpoints: Maryland state line southwest of Newark to the Pennsylvania state line at Claymont
i-95/de.description: Delaware's I-95 is a short, heavily traveled tolled stretch running from the Maryland line past Newark and through downtown Wilmington to the Pennsylvania line. Through trucks can bypass the Wilmington viaduct on I-495 along the Delaware River, and the corridor connects directly to the New Jersey Turnpike via I-295 at the Delaware Memorial Bridge.

i-95/ma.endpoints: Rhode Island state line at Attleboro north around Boston to the New Hampshire state line at Salisbury
i-95/ma.description: Rather than entering Boston, I-95 swings around the city on the Route 128 beltway through Waltham, Lexington, and Peabody before running up the North Shore to the New Hampshire line. The 128 section is dense with commuter traffic and closely spaced interchanges, while the stretches at both state lines are comparatively open.

i-95/md.endpoints: Woodrow Wilson Bridge at the District of Columbia line northeast to the Delaware state line at Elkton
i-95/md.description: I-95 in Maryland runs from the Wilson Bridge around the east side of Washington, then northeast past Laurel and Columbia into Baltimore, where the mainline uses the Fort McHenry Tunnel — hazmat loads must divert around it. Northeast of Baltimore the tolled corridor passes the Aberdeen area and crosses the Susquehanna River on the way to Delaware, carrying some of the heaviest freight volumes on the East Coast.

i-95/me.endpoints: New Hampshire state line at Kittery north to the Canadian border at Houlton
i-95/me.description: I-95 runs the length of Maine from Kittery through the Portland area and Bangor to the Canadian border at Houlton, with much of the southern half operating as the tolled Maine Turnpike. North of Bangor is one of the longest low-service rural interstate stretches in the eastern US, so top off fuel before heading up; Portland's waterfront and Bangor anchor most of the state's freight activity.

i-95/nh.endpoints: Massachusetts state line at Seabrook to the Maine state line at the Piscataqua River Bridge in Portsmouth
i-95/nh.description: New Hampshire's I-95 is a short tolled run of about 16 miles along the Seacoast, from Seabrook past Portsmouth and over the high Piscataqua River Bridge into Maine. It funnels all coastal New England-to-Maine traffic through a single toll plaza at Hampton, which backs up badly on summer weekends.

i-95/nj.endpoints: Delaware River crossing from the Pennsylvania Turnpike near Florence north to the George Washington Bridge at Fort Lee
i-95/nj.description: I-95 in New Jersey follows the New Jersey Turnpike from the Pennsylvania Turnpike connector bridge north past Newark Airport and the Port Newark-Elizabeth container port to the George Washington Bridge. The Turnpike's dual-dual layout separates trucks into outer lanes for much of the run, and the stretch through Elizabeth and Newark is among the busiest truck corridors in the nation.

i-95/ny.endpoints: George Washington Bridge at the New Jersey line to the Connecticut state line at Port Chester
i-95/ny.description: I-95 in New York crosses the George Washington Bridge, fights through the notoriously congested Cross Bronx Expressway, then follows the tolled New England Thruway through New Rochelle to the Connecticut line. The Cross Bronx is consistently ranked among the worst truck bottlenecks in the country, so time this stretch carefully.

i-95/ri.endpoints: Connecticut state line at Hopkinton northeast to the Massachusetts state line at Pawtucket
i-95/ri.description: I-95 crosses Rhode Island from quiet woods at the Connecticut line into the dense Providence metro, passing Warwick and T.F. Green Airport before threading directly through downtown Providence and Pawtucket. I-295 offers a western bypass of the city, and I-195 splits off downtown toward New Bedford and Cape Cod.

i-20/sc.endpoints: Georgia state line at the Savannah River near Augusta to its eastern terminus at I-95 near Florence
i-20/sc.description: I-20 crosses central South Carolina from the Augusta area northeast through Columbia, ending at I-95 near Florence. It links Georgia freight to the I-95 corridor with mostly rural running outside the Columbia metro, where it junctions both I-26 and I-77.

i-24/ky.endpoints: Ohio River crossing from Illinois at Paducah to the Tennessee state line near Clarksville
i-24/ky.description: I-24 cuts southeast across western Kentucky from the Ohio River at Paducah past Hopkinsville toward Nashville. It is a lightly developed rural stretch that carries heavy Chicago-to-Southeast through traffic and overlaps I-69 east of Paducah.

i-24/tn.endpoints: Kentucky state line near Clarksville to its eastern terminus at I-75 in Chattanooga
i-24/tn.description: I-24 runs southeast through Nashville and Murfreesboro to Chattanooga, ending at I-75. Drivers face heavy metro congestion around Nashville and the steep Monteagle grade over the Cumberland Plateau, one of the toughest mountain descents in the Southeast.

i-26/nc.endpoints: Tennessee state line at Sams Gap to the South Carolina state line near Columbus
i-26/nc.description: I-26 descends through the Blue Ridge Mountains past Asheville, with long steep grades on both sides of the city, including the sustained downgrade toward the South Carolina line at Saluda. It connects the Tennessee Tri-Cities to the Upstate South Carolina manufacturing belt.

i-26/sc.endpoints: North Carolina state line near Landrum to its eastern terminus at Charleston
i-26/sc.description: I-26 is South Carolina's main port corridor, running from the Upstate near Spartanburg through Columbia to the Port of Charleston container terminals. Drayage and intermodal traffic is heavy on the eastern end between I-95 and North Charleston.

i-26/tn.endpoints: Western terminus at I-81 near Kingsport to the North Carolina state line at Sams Gap
i-26/tn.description: I-26 links I-81 at Kingsport through Johnson City into the mountains toward Asheville. The Tri-Cities section is moderately busy urban freeway before the route climbs to Sams Gap on the North Carolina line.

i-40/nc.endpoints: Tennessee state line in the Pigeon River Gorge to its eastern terminus at Wilmington
i-40/nc.description: I-40 spans North Carolina from the narrow, rockslide-prone Pigeon River Gorge at the Tennessee line through Asheville, the Piedmont Triad, and the Raleigh-Durham metro to the Port of Wilmington. Expect mountain grades in the west and steady metro congestion from Winston-Salem through Raleigh.

i-40/tn.endpoints: Mississippi River crossing from Arkansas at Memphis to the North Carolina state line in the Pigeon River Gorge
i-40/tn.description: I-40 crosses the full width of Tennessee, tying the Memphis river and rail hub to Nashville and Knoxville before climbing into the Smokies at the North Carolina line. It is one of the busiest coast-to-coast truck corridors in the country, with major congestion in all three metros and plateau grades around Cookeville.

i-55/tn.endpoints: Mississippi state line in south Memphis to the Mississippi River crossing into Arkansas at the Memphis-Arkansas Bridge
i-55/tn.description: I-55's short Tennessee section runs entirely through southwest Memphis, connecting Mississippi to the Memphis-Arkansas Bridge over the Mississippi River. It serves heavy industrial and intermodal traffic around the Memphis terminals and the I-240 loop.

i-59/tn.endpoints: Approach from the Georgia state line to its northern terminus at I-24 near Wildwood, just southwest of Chattanooga
i-59/tn.description: I-59 reaches its northern terminus at I-24 in the far corner of the Chattanooga area, at the end of the Birmingham-to-Chattanooga corridor. Nearly all of the route's mileage lies in Georgia and Alabama, so this segment is a very short valley approach feeding I-24 traffic into Chattanooga.
i-59/tn.verified: osm-2026-07-13 (route stays out of state; cities from cross-border buffer)

i-64/ky.endpoints: Ohio River crossing from Indiana at Louisville to the West Virginia state line near Catlettsburg
i-64/ky.description: I-64 crosses central Kentucky from Louisville through Frankfort and the north side of Lexington, then runs long rural miles through the eastern hills to the Ashland area. The Louisville spaghetti-junction interchange with I-65 and I-71 is a known chokepoint; services thin out east of Winchester.

i-64/va.endpoints: West Virginia state line near Covington to its eastern terminus at I-664 in Chesapeake
i-64/va.description: I-64 runs from the Alleghany Mountains through Charlottesville and Richmond to the Port of Virginia terminals in Hampton Roads, including the Hampton Roads Bridge-Tunnel between Hampton and Norfolk. It carries heavy port drayage on the eastern end and overlaps I-81 between Lexington and Staunton in the Shenandoah Valley.

i-64/wv.endpoints: Kentucky state line near Kenova to the Virginia state line east of White Sulphur Springs
i-64/wv.description: I-64 crosses southern West Virginia from Huntington through Charleston, then shares the tolled West Virginia Turnpike with I-77 south to Beckley before turning east through the mountains to Lewisburg. Expect sustained grades, curves, and toll plazas on the Turnpike overlap.

i-65/ky.endpoints: Tennessee state line near Franklin to the Ohio River crossing into Indiana at Louisville
i-65/ky.description: I-65 runs north through Bowling Green and Elizabethtown to Louisville, one of the heaviest freight lanes between the Midwest and the South. Louisville's downtown river crossing and the Kennedy Interchange with I-64 and I-71 are the main congestion points.

i-65/tn.endpoints: Alabama state line near Ardmore to the Kentucky state line north of Portland
i-65/tn.description: I-65 climbs north out of the Alabama hill country through the fast-growing Franklin and Brentwood suburbs into Nashville, where it threads the downtown loop with I-40 and I-24. Rush-hour congestion through Williamson County and downtown Nashville is severe; I-840 offers a southern bypass.

i-69/ky.endpoints: Tennessee state line at Fulton to the Ohio River near Henderson at the Indiana line
i-69/ky.description: I-69 through western Kentucky follows upgraded former parkways, running from Fulton northeast to a short overlap with I-24, then north past Madisonville to Henderson on the Ohio River. It is a rural, lightly trafficked corridor with long gaps between full-service truck stops.

i-69/tn.endpoints: Mississippi state line south of Memphis to the current end of signed route in the Memphis area; the corridor toward the Kentucky line at South Fulton is largely unbuilt
i-69/tn.description: I-69 in Tennessee is currently signed along existing Memphis freeways, sharing pavement with I-55 and I-240 through the metro. The planned standalone corridor north toward Union City and the Kentucky line remains incomplete, so through traffic uses US highways beyond Memphis.

i-70/oh.endpoints: Indiana state line west of Lewisburg to the West Virginia state line at the Ohio River near Bridgeport
i-70/oh.description: I-70 crosses Ohio through the north side of Dayton, Springfield, and Columbus before rolling through hillier terrain past Zanesville to the Ohio River at Wheeling. The Columbus stretch between the I-270 beltway legs is a major national freight crossroads where I-70 meets I-71.

i-70/pa.endpoints: West Virginia state line at West Alexander to the Maryland state line at Warfordsburg
i-70/pa.description: I-70 crosses southwestern Pennsylvania through Washington and New Stanton, then rides the tolled Pennsylvania Turnpike (I-76) east to Breezewood, where through traffic must exit onto surface streets with traffic lights before continuing south to Maryland. The older non-Turnpike sections have short ramps and rolling grades.

i-70/wv.endpoints: Ohio state line at the Ohio River in Wheeling to the Pennsylvania state line near Valley Grove
i-70/wv.description: I-70's short Northern Panhandle segment passes directly through Wheeling, including the Wheeling Tunnel and a tight downtown stretch. The I-470 bypass to the south lets through trucks avoid the tunnel and city interchanges.

i-71/ky.endpoints: Southern terminus in Louisville to the Ohio River crossing at Covington into Cincinnati
i-71/ky.description: I-71 links Louisville and Cincinnati along a rolling rural corridor that parallels the Ohio River, joining I-75 at Walton for the busy combined run through Florence and Covington to the Brent Spence Bridge. The bridge approach into Cincinnati is one of the most congested truck bottlenecks in the region.

i-71/oh.endpoints: Ohio River at Cincinnati to its northern terminus at I-90 in Cleveland
i-71/oh.description: I-71 is Ohio's main diagonal, connecting Cincinnati, Columbus, and Cleveland with mostly flat, three-lane rural running between the metros. Congestion concentrates on the Columbus inner belt area and the approach into Cleveland past Strongsville.

i-74/oh.endpoints: Indiana state line near Harrison to its eastern terminus at I-75 in Cincinnati
i-74/oh.description: I-74's short Ohio segment drops from the Indiana line into Cincinnati, ending at I-75 just north of downtown. It funnels Indianapolis-Cincinnati freight through hilly western Hamilton County and the I-275 beltway interchange.

i-75/ky.endpoints: Tennessee state line at Jellico to the Ohio River crossing at Covington into Cincinnati
i-75/ky.description: I-75 climbs out of the Cumberland Mountains at Jellico and runs north through Richmond, Lexington, and Georgetown to the Cincinnati suburbs. Watch for grades and truck speed advisories in the southern mountains and heavy congestion at the Brent Spence Bridge approach in Covington.

i-75/oh.endpoints: Ohio River crossing at Cincinnati to the Michigan state line at Toledo
i-75/oh.description: I-75 runs the length of western Ohio, tying together the Cincinnati, Dayton, and Toledo industrial corridors on one of the busiest north-south truck routes in the country. The flat, heavily traveled lane serves major auto and manufacturing freight, with congestion in downtown Cincinnati and Dayton and at the Ohio Turnpike junction near Toledo.

i-75/tn.endpoints: Georgia state line at Chattanooga to the Kentucky state line at Jellico
i-75/tn.description: I-75 runs from Chattanooga through Cleveland to Knoxville, where it overlaps I-40 through a congested downtown corridor, then climbs into the Cumberland Mountains toward Jellico. The northern mountain section has long grades and is prone to fog and winter closures.

i-76/oh.endpoints: Western terminus at I-71 near Westfield Center to the Pennsylvania state line east of Youngstown
i-76/oh.description: I-76 runs east from I-71 through Akron, then joins the tolled Ohio Turnpike mainline south of Youngstown for the run into Pennsylvania. The central Akron interchange complex with I-77 sees regular congestion and construction.

i-76/pa.endpoints: Ohio state line near Petersburg to the New Jersey state line at the Walt Whitman Bridge in Philadelphia
i-76/pa.description: I-76 follows the tolled Pennsylvania Turnpike across the state, passing north and east of Pittsburgh through Cranberry Township and Monroeville, then over a series of Allegheny ridge tunnels before skirting south of Harrisburg. East of Valley Forge it becomes the free Schuylkill Expressway, a tight and heavily congested approach into Philadelphia.

i-77/nc.endpoints: South Carolina state line south of Charlotte to the Virginia state line north of Mount Airy
i-77/nc.description: I-77 runs through the heart of Charlotte and its Lake Norman suburbs, one of the most congested urban corridors in the Carolinas, with tolled express lanes north of the city. Past Statesville and the I-40 junction, it climbs toward the Blue Ridge at the Virginia line.

i-77/oh.endpoints: Ohio River crossing from West Virginia at Marietta to its northern terminus at I-90 in Cleveland
i-77/oh.description: I-77 runs from the Ohio River at Marietta north through Canton and Akron to downtown Cleveland. The southern half is hilly and rural with long gaps between services, while the Canton-Akron-Cleveland stretch is a steady industrial freight corridor.

i-77/sc.endpoints: Southern terminus at I-26 near Cayce to the North Carolina state line south of Charlotte
i-77/sc.description: I-77 begins at I-26 outside Columbia and runs north past Rock Hill into the Charlotte metro. It is a straightforward rolling corridor that funnels Columbia and Charleston-bound freight toward Charlotte, with growing suburban traffic north of Rock Hill.

i-77/va.endpoints: North Carolina state line at Lambsburg to the West Virginia state line at the East River Mountain Tunnel
i-77/va.description: I-77 crosses the Virginia mountains with two signature challenges for trucks: the long Fancy Gap grade climbing from the North Carolina line, notorious for fog and runaway-truck ramps, and the East River Mountain Tunnel at the West Virginia line. It briefly overlaps I-81 near Wytheville, the region's main service hub.

i-77/wv.endpoints: Virginia state line at the East River Mountain Tunnel near Bluefield to the Ohio River crossing at Parkersburg
i-77/wv.description: I-77 crosses West Virginia via the tolled West Virginia Turnpike from Bluefield through Beckley to Charleston, a twisting mountain section with steep grades and multiple toll plazas. North of Charleston the route flattens somewhat on its way to the Ohio River at Parkersburg.

i-78/pa.endpoints: Western terminus at I-81 near Jonestown to the New Jersey state line at the Delaware River south of Easton
i-78/pa.description: I-78 splits from I-81 in Lebanon County and runs east past the massive Lehigh Valley warehouse belt around Allentown and Bethlehem to the Delaware River. It is a primary lane for freight heading to New York City and northern New Jersey, with dense truck volume and frequent slowdowns through the Lehigh Valley.

i-79/pa.endpoints: West Virginia state line south of Waynesburg to its northern terminus at I-90 in Erie
i-79/pa.description: I-79 runs the length of western Pennsylvania, passing just west of Pittsburgh and through the Cranberry Township growth corridor before long rural miles north to Erie. It ties the Pittsburgh metro to I-80, the Turnpike, and the Lake Erie ports.

i-79/wv.endpoints: Southern terminus at I-77 in Charleston to the Pennsylvania state line north of Morgantown
i-79/wv.description: I-79 climbs northeast from Charleston through the hills past Clarksburg and Fairmont to Morgantown, where it meets I-68. It is a rolling, mostly rural corridor with long distances between major services and winter weather exposure in the higher sections.

i-80/oh.endpoints: Indiana state line near Montpelier to the Pennsylvania state line east of Hubbard
i-80/oh.description: I-80 crosses northern Ohio mostly on the tolled Ohio Turnpike, skirting south of Toledo and Cleveland with wide-open, flat running and full-service plazas. East of the Turnpike split it becomes a free route through the Youngstown area before entering Pennsylvania.

i-80/pa.endpoints: Ohio state line near Sharon to the New Jersey state line at the Delaware Water Gap
i-80/pa.description: I-80 crosses the sparsely populated ridges of northern Pennsylvania, a long rural haul with sustained grades, frequent winter weather, and big gaps between services. It intersects I-81 and the Northeast Extension (I-476) near the Hazleton warehouse cluster before descending to the Delaware Water Gap.

i-81/pa.endpoints: Maryland state line near Greencastle to the New York state line near Great Bend
i-81/pa.description: I-81 runs the Cumberland and Wyoming valleys from the Maryland line through Harrisburg, Wilkes-Barre, and Scranton, serving one of the densest warehouse and distribution corridors in the Northeast. Truck volume is very heavy from Carlisle through Harrisburg, and the route climbs steadily in the Pocono-region sections.

i-81/tn.endpoints: Southern terminus at I-40 near Dandridge to the Virginia state line at Bristol
i-81/tn.description: I-81 begins at I-40 east of Knoxville and runs northeast through the Tri-Cities region past Kingsport to Bristol on the Virginia line. It funnels I-40 freight into the heavily trucked Shenandoah corridor and meets I-26 near Kingsport.

i-81/va.endpoints: Tennessee state line at Bristol to the West Virginia state line north of Winchester
i-81/va.description: I-81 runs the full length of Virginia's Shenandoah and Great Valleys, from Bristol past Roanoke and Harrisonburg to Winchester, and carries some of the heaviest truck percentages of any rural interstate in the East. Rolling grades, high truck density, and limited passing capacity make it a demanding drive; it overlaps I-77 near Wytheville and I-64 near Staunton.

i-81/wv.endpoints: Virginia state line south of Martinsburg to the Maryland state line at the Potomac River near Williamsport
i-81/wv.description: I-81's short Eastern Panhandle segment passes through Martinsburg, a growing distribution-center hub between the Virginia and Maryland lines. It is a busy connector on the continuous I-81 freight corridor with no other interstate junctions in-state.

i-83/pa.endpoints: Maryland state line south of Shrewsbury to its northern terminus at I-81 north of Harrisburg
i-83/pa.description: I-83 climbs from the Maryland line through York to Harrisburg, crossing the Susquehanna River and ending at I-81. It links Baltimore freight to the central Pennsylvania distribution belt, with older, tight interchanges through the Harrisburg area.

i-84/pa.endpoints: Western terminus at I-81 in Scranton to the New York state line near Matamoras
i-84/pa.description: I-84 begins at I-81 in Scranton and runs east across the wooded Pocono plateau to the Delaware River at the New York line. It is a lightly developed rural stretch with winter weather exposure and few services between Scranton and Milford.

i-85/nc.endpoints: South Carolina state line near Grover to the Virginia state line north of Wise
i-85/nc.description: I-85 is the spine of the Piedmont manufacturing crescent, running from Gastonia through Charlotte, the Salisbury-Kannapolis corridor, Greensboro, and Durham before turning rural toward Virginia. It overlaps I-40 between Greensboro and Hillsborough and carries constant heavy truck traffic through the Charlotte metro.

i-85/sc.endpoints: Georgia state line at Lake Hartwell to the North Carolina state line near Blacksburg
i-85/sc.description: I-85 crosses the Upstate through the Greenville-Spartanburg manufacturing corridor, passing the BMW plant at Greer and the inland port that feed steady container and auto-parts truck traffic. It is one of the busiest freight lanes in the Southeast, linking Atlanta to Charlotte.

i-85/va.endpoints: North Carolina state line near Bracey to its northern terminus at I-95 in Petersburg
i-85/va.description: I-85 runs a quiet, mostly rural course through Southside Virginia from the North Carolina line to Petersburg, where it merges into I-95 toward Richmond. Services are sparse between South Hill and the Petersburg area.

i-86/pa.endpoints: Western terminus at I-90 near Harborcreek, east of Erie, to the New York state line
i-86/pa.description: I-86's short Pennsylvania stub begins at I-90 just east of Erie and immediately crosses into New York toward Jamestown. It serves as the western gateway to the Southern Tier Expressway corridor across upstate New York.

i-90/oh.endpoints: Indiana state line near Montpelier to the Pennsylvania state line at Conneaut
i-90/oh.description: I-90 shares the tolled Ohio Turnpike with I-80 across northwest Ohio past Toledo, then splits at Elyria to run free through downtown Cleveland and along the Lake Erie shore to Conneaut. The Cleveland section includes the sharp Dead Man's Curve on the innerbelt, a posted slow zone for trucks, and lake-effect snow is a factor east of the city.

i-90/pa.endpoints: Ohio state line near West Springfield to the New York state line near North East
i-90/pa.description: I-90 crosses Pennsylvania's short Lake Erie shoreline strip, passing just south of Erie where it meets I-79. The corridor sits squarely in the lake-effect snow belt, with sudden whiteout conditions common in winter.

i-95/nc.endpoints: South Carolina state line near Rowland to the Virginia state line north of Roanoke Rapids
i-95/nc.description: I-95 crosses the flat eastern North Carolina coastal plain past Fayetteville, Wilson, and Rocky Mount, crossing I-40 at Benson. It is a steady through-freight lane with long rural stretches, ongoing widening work, and truck-stop clusters at the major junction towns.

i-95/pa.endpoints: Delaware state line near Marcus Hook to the New Jersey state line at the Delaware River-Turnpike Bridge near Bristol
i-95/pa.description: I-95 hugs the Delaware River through Chester and downtown Philadelphia, a dense urban corridor serving the Philadelphia port terminals and refineries with constant congestion and older, tight interchanges. Through traffic now follows I-95 onto the Pennsylvania Turnpike connector bridge into New Jersey at Bristol.

i-95/sc.endpoints: Georgia state line at the Savannah River near Hardeeville to the North Carolina state line near Dillon
i-95/sc.description: I-95 crosses South Carolina's rural lowcountry and Pee Dee regions, with Florence at the I-20 junction serving as the main fuel and service hub. The corridor is a long, flat through-run between Savannah and the North Carolina line, with older narrow sections under staged widening.

i-95/va.endpoints: North Carolina state line near Skippers to the Potomac River crossing at the Woodrow Wilson Bridge toward Maryland
i-95/va.description: I-95 runs from the rural Southside through Petersburg and downtown Richmond, then into the notoriously congested Fredericksburg-to-Springfield stretch feeding Washington DC, with reversible tolled express lanes in the northern section. The I-295 loop lets through trucks bypass Richmond and Petersburg.

i-5/or.endpoints: California state line at Siskiyou Summit to the Washington state line at the Columbia River in Portland
i-5/or.description: I-5 runs south to north the length of western Oregon, climbing over Siskiyou Summit near the California line before descending through Medford, the Willamette Valley, and into Portland. It is the West Coast's main freight spine, mixing long rural valley stretches with heavy metro congestion around Portland and mountain grades and winter chain requirements at the southern end.

i-5/wa.endpoints: Oregon state line at the Columbia River in Vancouver to the Canadian border at Blaine
i-5/wa.description: I-5 in Washington runs south to north from the Columbia River crossing at Vancouver through the Tacoma and Seattle metro areas to the Canadian border at Blaine. It carries port traffic from Tacoma and Seattle plus cross-border freight, with some of the heaviest urban congestion on the West Coast between Tacoma and Everett.

i-15/id.endpoints: Utah state line south of Malad City to the Montana state line at Monida Pass
i-15/id.description: I-15 crosses eastern Idaho south to north, linking the Salt Lake City freight corridor to Montana through Pocatello and Idaho Falls. Beyond Idaho Falls it is a long rural climb through open high country to Monida Pass at the Montana line, with limited services.

i-15/mt.endpoints: Idaho state line at Monida Pass to the Canadian border at Sweetgrass
i-15/mt.description: I-15 runs south to north across western Montana from Monida Pass through Butte, Helena, and Great Falls to the Sweetgrass border crossing, the busiest truck port of entry between Montana and Canada. Expect mountain grades around Butte and Helena, long rural gaps between services, and winter closures in high country.

i-25/wy.endpoints: Colorado state line south of Cheyenne to its northern terminus at I-90 near Buffalo
i-25/wy.description: I-25 runs south to north through eastern Wyoming from the Colorado line at Cheyenne through Casper to its end at I-90 near Buffalo. It is a high-plains route serving energy and ranch freight, with long stretches between towns and frequent high-wind advisories.

i-29/nd.endpoints: South Dakota state line south of Fargo to the Canadian border at Pembina
i-29/nd.description: I-29 runs south to north up the flat Red River Valley through Fargo and Grand Forks to the Pembina border crossing, a major truck port of entry into Manitoba. The route is straight and level agricultural country, but winter ground blizzards and closures are a real hazard.

i-29/sd.endpoints: Iowa state line near North Sioux City to the North Dakota state line north of Sisseton
i-29/sd.description: I-29 runs south to north along the eastern edge of South Dakota, connecting Sioux City to Fargo through Sioux Falls, Brookings, and Watertown. Sioux Falls, where it crosses I-90, is the main freight hub on the route; north of Watertown services thin out across open farmland.

i-39/wi.endpoints: Illinois state line south of Beloit to its northern terminus at US 51 near Merrill
i-39/wi.description: I-39 runs south to north through central Wisconsin, overlapping I-90 from the Illinois line through Janesville and Madison before splitting north at Portage toward Stevens Point and Wausau. It is the main freight route between the Chicago-Rockford corridor and the paper and manufacturing towns of north-central Wisconsin.

i-43/wi.endpoints: Southern terminus at I-39/I-90 in Beloit to its northern terminus at I-41 in Green Bay
i-43/wi.description: I-43 lies entirely within Wisconsin, running northeast from I-39/I-90 at Beloit through downtown Milwaukee, then up the Lake Michigan shore through Sheboygan and Manitowoc to Green Bay. It serves the Port of Milwaukee and the lakeshore manufacturing belt, with metro congestion concentrated around the Milwaukee interchanges.

i-80/wy.endpoints: Utah state line at Evanston to the Nebraska state line at Pine Bluffs
i-80/wy.description: I-80 crosses southern Wyoming west to east through Rock Springs, Laramie, and Cheyenne, topping out at Sherman Summit, the highest point on the entire route. It is one of the country's heaviest transcontinental truck corridors, notorious for high-wind blowover restrictions and winter closures, especially around Elk Mountain between Rawlins and Laramie.

i-84/id.endpoints: Oregon state line at the Snake River near Ontario to the Utah state line near Juniper
i-84/id.description: I-84 runs west to east across southern Idaho, through the Treasure Valley cities of Caldwell, Nampa, Meridian, and Boise, then along the Snake River Plain past Twin Falls toward Utah. It links Pacific Northwest freight to the Salt Lake City hub, with agricultural traffic heavy through the Magic Valley and long rural gaps southeast of Burley.

i-84/or.endpoints: Western terminus at I-5 in Portland to the Idaho state line at Ontario
i-84/or.description: I-84 begins at I-5 in Portland and runs east through the Columbia River Gorge, then across eastern Oregon over Cabbage Hill (Emigrant Hill) near Pendleton and the Blue Mountains to the Idaho line at Ontario. The Gorge brings winter ice and wind closures, and Cabbage Hill's steep 6 percent grades are a well-known descent for loaded trucks.

i-86/id.endpoints: Western terminus at I-84 near Heyburn to its eastern terminus at I-15 near Pocatello
i-86/id.description: I-86 is a short west-to-east connector entirely within southeastern Idaho, linking I-84 near Heyburn to I-15 at Pocatello along the Snake River Plain past American Falls. It is the through route for freight moving between Boise and the I-15 corridor, mostly rural with services concentrated at the Pocatello end.

i-90/id.endpoints: Washington state line at Post Falls to the Montana state line at Lookout Pass
i-90/id.description: I-90 crosses the Idaho panhandle west to east in about 75 miles, from the Washington line through Post Falls and Coeur d'Alene, then up the Silver Valley to Lookout Pass at the Montana border. The climb to Lookout Pass brings winter chain-up requirements and grades through the mountains east of Kellogg.

i-90/mt.endpoints: Idaho state line at Lookout Pass to the Wyoming state line north of Sheridan
i-90/mt.description: I-90's longest single-state stretch runs west to east across Montana through Missoula, Butte, Bozeman, and Billings, crossing the Continental Divide at Homestake Pass and climbing Bozeman Pass between Bozeman and Livingston. It is a mountain-grade corridor with long rural gaps between towns and frequent winter chain requirements.

i-90/sd.endpoints: Wyoming state line near Beulah to the Minnesota state line east of Sioux Falls
i-90/sd.description: I-90 crosses South Dakota west to east from the Black Hills at Rapid City over the Missouri River at Chamberlain to Sioux Falls, where it meets I-29. The route is mostly open prairie with long distances between full truck services, and winter wind and ice closures are common west of the river.

i-90/wa.endpoints: Western terminus at I-5 in Seattle to the Idaho state line east of Spokane Valley
i-90/wa.description: I-90 begins at I-5 in Seattle and runs east over Snoqualmie Pass, the state's main mountain freight crossing with winter chain requirements and traction closures, then across the Columbia Basin to Spokane. It carries port traffic from Seattle inland and is the primary east-west truck route across Washington.

i-90/wi.endpoints: Minnesota state line at La Crosse to the Illinois state line at Beloit
i-90/wi.description: I-90 enters Wisconsin west to east at the Mississippi River crossing in La Crosse, runs concurrent with I-94 from Tomah past Wisconsin Dells, then with I-39 through Madison and Janesville to the Illinois line at Beloit. It is the main link between the Twin Cities and Chicago, busy with through freight and tourist traffic around the Dells.

i-90/wy.endpoints: Montana state line north of Sheridan to the South Dakota state line near Beulah
i-90/wy.description: I-90 clips northeastern Wyoming, entering from Montana near Sheridan, meeting I-25 at Buffalo, and running east through Gillette and the Powder River Basin coal country to the South Dakota line. Coal and energy traffic is heavy around Gillette, and the open terrain brings strong crosswinds and winter closures.

i-94/mt.endpoints: Western terminus at I-90 near Billings to the North Dakota state line at Wibaux
i-94/mt.description: I-94 begins at I-90 just east of Billings and runs west to east down the Yellowstone River valley through Miles City and Glendive to the North Dakota line. It is a lightly traveled rural corridor with long gaps between fuel and repair services east of Billings.

i-94/nd.endpoints: Montana state line near Beach to the Minnesota state line at Fargo
i-94/nd.description: I-94 crosses North Dakota west to east through Dickinson, the Bismarck-Mandan area at the Missouri River, and Fargo, where it meets I-29 before crossing into Minnesota. It serves oil-patch and agricultural freight across open prairie, where ground blizzards and winter interstate closures are a routine hazard.

i-94/wi.endpoints: Minnesota state line at Hudson to the Illinois state line south of Kenosha
i-94/wi.description: I-94 enters Wisconsin from the Twin Cities at Hudson, runs southeast through Eau Claire, joins I-90 from Tomah through Madison, then continues east to Milwaukee and turns south along Lake Michigan past Racine and Kenosha to the Illinois line. It is the main Chicago-Milwaukee-Twin Cities freight corridor, with heavy metro congestion through the Milwaukee interchanges and the lakefront industrial belt.
